definition: The Alzheimer’s Association is an organization described here as providing a Helpline for family care partners of people living with dementia. In this context, it offers support resources and follow-up care consultations to help reduce caregiver stress and burden.

reasons: The packet states the study measured “efficacy” of follow-up Helpline consultations after an initial call, and reports that one call benefited 80% of callers, but it does not explicitly claim that the Helpline/resources “reduce caregiver stress and burden.”

The packet supports that the Alzheimer’s Association has a Helpline and offers follow-up care consultations after an initial call, but it does not explicitly support the broader claim that the organization provides general support resources in this context.

The statement that these consultations are offered to help reduce caregiver stress and burden goes beyond the packet’s wording; the packet says caregivers experience high stress and burden and that the study evaluated efficacy, but it does not directly state this outcome as a supported description of the organization’s service.
